links.outcome: Response consistency across matched clinician-language versus patient-language prompt phrasings, expert-rated clinical confidence
links.effect: Clinically reliable: 89.3% clinician-language vs 91.3% patient-language; cumulative OR 0.78 (95% CI 0.57-1.06; p=0.115); language-by-model interaction p=0.422. Some secondary scores higher for patient-language.
links.quote: Patient-language phrasing was not significantly associated with overall GCCS (cumulative odds ratio 0.78, 95% confidence interval 0.57-1.06; p = 0.115), and the language-by-model interaction was not significant (p = 0.422).

screen.reason: Evaluates LLM performance and clinical safety differences between patient-language and clinician-language triage prompt inputs without testing a specific organizational safeguard or deployment practice.
